<CodeSample>

```python
from mistralai.client import Mistral
import os


with Mistral(
    api_key=os.getenv("MISTRAL_API_KEY", ""),
) as mistral:

    res = mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.projects.list(page_size=50, page=1)

    # Handle response
    print(res)


```

<ExpandablePropertyTitle slot="title">

##### ownership \{#operation-search_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluations_v2_evaluation_slug_runs_search_post_request_evaluationrunfilterinput_ownership\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

OR-able group isolating the "runs I care about" default (created by me OR in my starred projects).

Kept separate from the plain generic filters so it can OR internally while still AND-ing with
everything else. The UI drives it via two sugar chips: "Created by me" writes `creator_ids`, and
"Starred projects" sets `starred_by_me`. Dropping a chip clears its term and the OR collapses to the
remaining one; dropping both leaves the group empty (no ownership scoping).

`starred_by_me` is resolved server-side against the caller's favorites, so the client never has to
page through projects to collect starred ids — and a caller with zero starred projects correctly
matches no runs (rather than falling through to the whole workspace). `project_ids` remains for
explicit, caller-supplied project scoping.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

  hasExpandableContent={true}
  expandByDefault={false}
>

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ClassificationStatisticSpec \{#operation-search_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluations_v2_evaluation_slug_runs_search_post_responses_200_application-json_runs_paginatedresultevaluationrunv2response_results_evaluationrunv2response_evaluators_evaluatorv2_statistics_classificationstatisticspec\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

<ExpandableBreakoutProperties slot="properties">

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ClassificationStatisticSpec \{#operation-search_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluations_v2_evaluation_slug_runs_search_post_responses_200_application-json_runs_paginatedresultevaluationrunv2response_results_evaluationrunv2response_run_evaluators_evaluatorv2_statistics_classificationstatisticspec\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-search_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluations_v2_evaluation_slug_runs_search_post_responses_200_application-json_runs_paginatedresultevaluationrunv2response_results_evaluationrunv2response_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

}

run();

<ExpandablePropertyTitle slot="title">

##### ownership \{#operation-search_all_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_search_post_request_evaluationrunfilterinput_ownership\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

OR-able group isolating the "runs I care about" default (created by me OR in my starred projects).

Kept separate from the plain generic filters so it can OR internally while still AND-ing with
everything else. The UI drives it via two sugar chips: "Created by me" writes `creator_ids`, and
"Starred projects" sets `starred_by_me`. Dropping a chip clears its term and the OR collapses to the
remaining one; dropping both leaves the group empty (no ownership scoping).

`starred_by_me` is resolved server-side against the caller's favorites, so the client never has to
page through projects to collect starred ids — and a caller with zero starred projects correctly
matches no runs (rather than falling through to the whole workspace). `project_ids` remains for
explicit, caller-supplied project scoping.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

  hasExpandableContent={true}
  expandByDefault={false}
>

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ClassificationStatisticSpec \{#operation-search_all_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_search_post_responses_200_application-json_runs_paginatedresultevaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_results_evaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_evaluators_evaluatorv2_statistics_classificationstatisticspec\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ClassificationStatisticSpec \{#operation-search_all_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_search_post_responses_200_application-json_runs_paginatedresultevaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_results_evaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_run_evaluators_evaluatorv2_statistics_classificationstatisticspec\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-search_all_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_search_post_responses_200_application-json_runs_paginatedresultevaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_results_evaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_statistics_numericstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-search_all_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_search_post_responses_200_application-json_runs_paginatedresultevaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_results_evaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-search_all_evaluation_runs_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_search_post_responses_200_application-json_runs_paginatedresultevaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_results_evaluationrunv2withrefsresponse_statistics_categoricalstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

const mistral = new Mistral({

});

async function run() {

    runId: "c120b634-146a-4ae3-bd38-b7a168c4c8ce",
  });

  console.log(result);
}

run();

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ClassificationStatisticSpec \{#operation-get_evaluation_run_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_get_responses_200_application-json_evaluators_evaluatorv2_statistics_classificationstatisticspec\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

#### ClassificationStatisticSpec \{#operation-get_evaluation_run_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_get_responses_200_application-json_run_evaluators_evaluatorv2_statistics_classificationstatisticspec\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-get_evaluation_run_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_get_responses_200_application-json_statistics_numericstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-get_evaluation_run_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_get_responses_200_application-json_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-get_evaluation_run_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_get_responses_200_application-json_statistics_categoricalstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

<CodeSample>

```typescript
import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

const mistral = new Mistral({
  apiKey: "MISTRAL_API_KEY",
});

async function run() {
  const result = await mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.runs.getStatistics({
    runId: "a38473a2-532a-4cb8-9320-a7f617d16595",
  });

  console.log(result);
}

run();

```

<SDKVersionCodeSample>
<div data-version="v2">
<CodeSample>

```python
from mistralai.client import Mistral
import os


with Mistral(
    api_key=os.getenv("MISTRAL_API_KEY", ""),
) as mistral:

    res = mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.runs.get_statistics(run_id="a38473a2-532a-4cb8-9320-a7f617d16595")

    # Handle response
    print(res)


```

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-get_single_evaluation_run_statistics_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_statistics_get_responses_200_application-json_statistics_numericstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-get_single_evaluation_run_statistics_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_statistics_get_responses_200_application-json_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-get_single_evaluation_run_statistics_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_statistics_get_responses_200_application-json_statistics_categoricalstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

<CodeSample>

```typescript
import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

const mistral = new Mistral({
  apiKey: "MISTRAL_API_KEY",
});

async function run() {
  const result = await mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.runs.computeStatistics({
    runId: "c5e1142f-de29-45b2-b29c-fe37e6509c8a",
  });

  console.log(result);
}

run();

```

from mistralai.client import Mistral
import os


with Mistral(
    api_key=os.getenv("MISTRAL_API_KEY", ""),
) as mistral:

    res = mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.runs.compute_statistics(run_id="c5e1142f-de29-45b2-b29c-fe37e6509c8a")

    # Handle response
    print(res)

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-compute_filtered_run_statistics_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_statistics_compute_post_responses_200_application-json_statistics_numericstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-compute_filtered_run_statistics_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_statistics_compute_post_responses_200_application-json_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-compute_filtered_run_statistics_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_statistics_compute_post_responses_200_application-json_statistics_categoricalstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

>

<CodeSample>

```typescript
import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

const mistral = new Mistral({
  apiKey: "MISTRAL_API_KEY",
});

async function run() {
  const result = await mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.records.get({
    runId: "4561f251-c638-4a33-8739-db876b032f73",
    recordId: "24b40e66-4e0d-4788-bb5a-df09239c7ba9",
  });

  console.log(result);
}

run();

```

</CodeSample>

<CodeSample>

```python
from mistralai.client import Mistral
import os


with Mistral(
    api_key=os.getenv("MISTRAL_API_KEY", ""),
) as mistral:

    res = mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.records.get(run_id="4561f251-c638-4a33-8739-db876b032f73", record_id="24b40e66-4e0d-4788-bb5a-df09239c7ba9")

    # Handle response
    print(res)


```

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-get_evaluation_run_record_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_record_id_get_responses_200_application-json_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_generations_evaluationrungenerationv2_statistics_numericstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-get_evaluation_run_record_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_record_id_get_responses_200_application-json_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_generations_evaluationrungenerationv2_statistics_categoricalstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-get_evaluation_run_record_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_record_id_get_responses_200_application-json_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

<CodeSample>

```typescript
import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

const mistral = new Mistral({
  apiKey: "MISTRAL_API_KEY",
});

async function run() {
  const result = await mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.records.search({
    runId: "3ec2a158-4bb7-4020-8a52-0f64a2745094",
  });

  console.log(result);
}

run();

```

<SDKVersionCodeSample>
<div data-version="v2">
<CodeSample>

```python
from mistralai.client import Mistral
import os


with Mistral(
    api_key=os.getenv("MISTRAL_API_KEY", ""),
) as mistral:

    res = mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.records.search(run_id="3ec2a158-4bb7-4020-8a52-0f64a2745094", page_size=50, page=1)

    # Handle response
    print(res)


```

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-search_evaluation_run_records_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_search_post_responses_200_application-json_records_paginatedresultevaluationrunrecordv2response_results_evaluationrunrecordv2response_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_generations_evaluationrungenerationv2_statistics_numericstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-search_evaluation_run_records_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_search_post_responses_200_application-json_records_paginatedresultevaluationrunrecordv2response_results_evaluationrunrecordv2response_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_generations_evaluationrungenerationv2_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-search_evaluation_run_records_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_search_post_responses_200_application-json_records_paginatedresultevaluationrunrecordv2response_results_evaluationrunrecordv2response_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_generations_evaluationrungenerationv2_statistics_categoricalstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-search_evaluation_run_records_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_search_post_responses_200_application-json_records_paginatedresultevaluationrunrecordv2response_results_evaluationrunrecordv2response_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_statistics_numericstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-search_evaluation_run_records_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_search_post_responses_200_application-json_records_paginatedresultevaluationrunrecordv2response_results_evaluationrunrecordv2response_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-search_evaluation_run_records_v2_v1_observability_evaluation_runs_v2_run_id_records_search_post_responses_200_application-json_records_paginatedresultevaluationrunrecordv2response_results_evaluationrunrecordv2response_output_record_evaluationrunoutputrecordv2_statistics_categoricalstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

from mistralai.client import Mistral

) as mistral:

    res = mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.optimizations.list(page_size=50, page=1)

    # Handle response
    print(res)

import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

    optimizationId: "fd7cc96b-0c32-4b79-b7e4-63786d9dcfea",

  console.log(result);
}

run();

<CodeSample>

```typescript
import { Mistral } from "@mistralai/mistralai";

const mistral = new Mistral({
  apiKey: "MISTRAL_API_KEY",
});

async function run() {
  const result = await mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.optimizations.listTrials({
    optimizationId: "54622d5d-6e77-4a86-9908-87b1f8f16424",
  });

  console.log(result);
}

run();

```

```python
from mistralai.client import Mistral
import os


with Mistral(
    api_key=os.getenv("MISTRAL_API_KEY", ""),
) as mistral:

    res = mistral.beta.observability.evaluations.optimizations.list_trials(optimization_id="54622d5d-6e77-4a86-9908-87b1f8f16424", page_size=50, page=1)

    # Handle response
    print(res)


```

#### ClassificationStatisticSpec \{#operation-list_optimization_trials_v1_observability_optimizations_optimization_id_trials_get_responses_200_application-json_trials_paginatedresultoptimizationtrialwithobservations_results_optimizationtrialwithobservations_observations_optimizationtrialobservation_run_evaluationrunv2response_evaluators_evaluatorv2_statistics_classificationstatisticspec\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

<ExpandableBreakoutTitle slot="title">

#### ClassificationStatisticSpec \{#operation-list_optimization_trials_v1_observability_optimizations_optimization_id_trials_get_responses_200_application-json_trials_paginatedresultoptimizationtrialwithobservations_results_optimizationtrialwithobservations_observations_optimizationtrialobservation_run_evaluationrunv2response_run_evaluators_evaluatorv2_statistics_classificationstatisticspec\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A classification metric (``precision``/``recall``/``f1``) over ``(expected, predicted)`` pairs.

The predicted label is the score ``value``; the expected label is read from the score ``metadata``
under ``expected_key`` (default ``"expected"``). Provide **exactly one** of ``positive_label`` (a
binary metric scored against that one class) or ``average`` (a multi-class averaging scheme).

``labels`` pins the class universe so filtered views keep a stable, comparable denominator.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-list_optimization_trials_v1_observability_optimizations_optimization_id_trials_get_responses_200_application-json_trials_paginatedresultoptimizationtrialwithobservations_results_optimizationtrialwithobservations_observations_optimizationtrialobservation_run_evaluationrunv2response_statistics_numericstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>

##### confusion_matrix \{#operation-list_optimization_trials_v1_observability_optimizations_optimization_id_trials_get_responses_200_application-json_trials_paginatedresultoptimizationtrialwithobservations_results_optimizationtrialwithobservations_observations_optimizationtrialobservation_run_evaluationrunv2response_statistics_categoricalstatistics_confusion_matrix\}

</ExpandablePropertyTitle>

<ExpandablePropertyDescription slot="description">

A confusion matrix over ``(expected, predicted)`` label pairs.

``matrix[i][j]`` is the number of samples whose expected label is ``labels[i]`` and predicted
label is ``labels[j]``. It is the complete, aggregatable representation: precision/recall/f1 for
any class derive from it, and matrices from several runs merge by element-wise sum.

</ExpandablePropertyDescription>

#### ScalarStatisticValue \{#operation-list_optimization_trials_v1_observability_optimizations_optimization_id_trials_get_responses_200_application-json_trials_paginatedresultoptimizationtrialwithobservations_results_optimizationtrialwithobservations_observations_optimizationtrialobservation_run_evaluationrunv2response_statistics_categoricalstatistics_values_scalarstatisticvalue\}

</ExpandableBreakoutTitle>

<ExpandableBreakoutDescription slot="description">

A single scalar computed run-level statistic: its canonical id and numeric value.

``value`` is ``None`` when the statistic is not evaluable (e.g. a ``sum`` or percentile over an
empty numeric sample). A declared ``count`` is always evaluable and is ``0`` on an empty sample.

The ``type`` discriminator lets future result shapes (e.g. a categorical ``categories`` or a
``distribution``) join a union without overloading this model; consumers dispatch on ``type``.

</ExpandableBreakoutDescription>
